evidence.title: Recommended Walking Route & Highlights
evidence.snippet: What to see: Start at Plaza Intendente Alvear (France Square). The white colonial church, built in 1732, is one of the oldest surviving churches in the city. evidence.title: Recommended Walking Route & Highlights
evidence.snippet: What to see: Step into this world-renowned city of the dead. It functions as an open-air museum filled with majestic neoclassical, Gothic, and Art Deco mausoleums where Argentina's historical elites, presidents, and poets rest—including the famous crypt of Eva "Evita" Perón.

evidence.title: Recommended Walking Route & Highlights

evidence.title: Recommended Walking Route & Highlights

evidence.title: Recommended Walking Route & Highlights
evidence.snippet: What to see: Walk toward Libertador Avenue to visit Argentina's premier public art gallery. It houses an incredible collection of European masters (including works by Degas, Renoir, and Rodin) alongside massive galleries of 19th- and 20th-century Argentine art.

evidence.title: Recommended Walking Route & Highlights
